items.stem: Under COSO, a monthly bank reconciliation that catches errors after they occur is best described as which control type?

options.rationale: Correct: it detects errors after the fact rather than preventing them.
Preventive controls stop errors before they happen.
Corrective controls fix an identified problem; reconciliation detects it.
This is a process-level activity, not an entity-level control.

items.stem: Which two conditions together make a control deficiency a material weakness? (Select TWO)

options.text: A reasonable possibility of a misstatement occurring
options.rationale: Correct: reasonable possibility of occurrence is one criterion.
Correct: a material magnitude is the other criterion.

options.text: The control is manual rather than automated
options.rationale: Manual controls are not automatically material weaknesses.

options.text: The deficiency was found by internal audit
options.rationale: Who finds it does not determine its severity.

items.stem: Which SOX section requires the CEO and CFO to certify the accuracy of financial reports each period?

options.rationale: Correct: Section 302 covers executive certification of reports.
Section 404 covers management's assessment of ICFR.
Section 101 established the PCAOB, not certification.
Section 906 addresses criminal certification, not the periodic report accuracy certification tested here.

items.explanation: Correct: Section 302 covers executive certification of reports.
